sentences.text:
Bench: K. Lakshman
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 Writ Petition No.21926 Of 2024
Oral Order

:
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 3, 5 and 6 and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing on behalf of respondent No.7.
2.

The petitioner herein is claiming that he is the absolute owner and possessor of the land bearing House No.1-66/1, admeasuring 109 square yards (Gramakantam) including tin-shed, situated at Zaffergadh Village and Grama Panchayath, Zaffergadh Mandal, Jangaon District, on the strength of a registered Gift Deed bearing document No.2403 of 2022, dated 24.06.2022.
He has demolished the structure with an intention to construct a house after obtaining permission from the Grama Panchayath, Zaffergadh.

In the meanwhile, respondent Nos.3 to 7 and Grama Panchayath,
Zaffergadh tried to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property.
Therefore, he has filed a writ petition vide W.P. No.6012 of 2023.

The said writ petition came up for hearing on 09.03.2023, on which date, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Grama Panchayath, Zaffergadh, KL,J has submitted that so far the Grama Panchayath has not taken any decision to lay the road from the land of the petitioner.

If the land of the petitioner is required, they will follow the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (for short 'Act, 2013'), and after verifying the documents submitted by the petitioner with regard to the ownership, they will initiate the proceedings.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Recording the said submission, this Court disposed of the said writ petition on 09.03.2023 directing Grama Panchayath, Zaffergadh, to strictly follow the provisions of the Act, 2013 before initiating any action against the subject property of the petitioner.

3. The grievance of the petitioner in the present writ petition is that on 06.08.2024, respondent Nos.3 to 7 came to the site and tried to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property under the guise of laying road.
In proof of the same, he has filed the photographs.
Thus, according to the petitioner, respondent Nos.3 to 7 are trying to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property without following due procedure laid down under law.
4. In the light of the said allegation, this Court directed learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue to get instructions from KL,J respondent Nos.2 to 6.

He has produced written instructions of respondent No.5, wherein it is stated that on 05.08.2024, MLA, Station Ghanpur has participated Kumara Swamy Thadem vs The State Of Telangana on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34154596/
1 in Swachadanam - Pachadanam rally programme at Zaffergadh with local villagers and during the said rally, the MLA passed through the muddy road pits filled with water due to heavy rains and raised the issue as to why the road was not laid even after completion of all sanctions.

entities.text: Kumara Swamy Thadem vs The State Of Telangana on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Villagers raised the issue of objections of the petitioner and immediately the MLA has instructed respondent No.3 to enquire into the matter and to ensure the work is completed.
The said written instructions are placed on record.
5. Perusal of the said written instructions would reveal that respondent Nos.3 and 5 under the pressure of local MLA tried to dispossess the petitioner with an intention to lay road.
The villagers cannot build pressure on the official respondents to do an illegal act of dispossessing the petitioner from the subject property without following due procedure laid down under law.

6. It is also apt to note that in the earlier round of litigation, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Grama Panchayath, Zaffergadh informed this Court that the Grama Panchayath, Zaffergadh has not taken any decision to lay the road from the land of KL,J the petitioner.
Thus, respondent Nos.2 to 7 cannot dispossess the petitioner without following the due procedure laid down under law.
7. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, on instructions, would submit that the son of the petitioner is making allegations against respondent Nos.2 to 6 and Villagers.

He has also produced written instructions of respondent No.7, wherein it is mentioned that the son of the petitioner called '100 dial' on 06.08.2024 at 2.17 p.m. and informed that the R&B Officials and RDO are trying to occupy their land and lay concrete road jeopardizing their rights.

On receiving the said call, respondent No.7 along with staff visited the spot and pacified the situation and further informed the petitioner and his son not to create public nuisance and if they are having any grievance, they may approach the competent Civil Court.
The said instructions are placed on record.
8. Admittedly, the subject property of the petitioner is in Grama Panchayath, Zaffergadh.

Respondent Nos.2 to 6 being Revenue Officials cannot lay road, and it is for the Grama Panchayath,
Zaffergadh to lay the road.

As discussed above, according to the Grama Panchayath, Zaffergadh,
there was no proposal to lay the road.
KL,J 9.
The aforesaid facts would reveal that respondent Nos.2 to 6 under the pressure of local MLA tried to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property on the pretext of laying road.
They cannot dispossess the petitioner without following due procedure laid down under law.
If the land of the petitioner is required for the purpose of laying road, they have to acquire the land of the petitioner in accordance with law.
It is also relevant to note that the subject land is Gramakantam land and the petitioner himself admitted the said fact in the writ affidavit.

10. In the light of the aforesaid discussion, this writ petition is disposed of directing respondent Nos.2 to 6 not to dispossess the petitioner from the subject property without following the due procedure laid down under law.

If the land of the petitioner is required for any public purpose including laying of road, liberty is granted to respondent Nos.2 to 6 to acquire the same by following Kumara Swamy Thadem vs The State Of Telangana on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34154596/
2 due procedure laid down under law.

sentences.text:
However, the petitioner shall not make construction over the subject property without obtaining prior permission from the Grama Panchayath, Zaffergadh,
failing which, liberty is granted to the said Grama Panchayath to take action against KL,J the petitioner in accordance with law.
In the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this writ petition shall stand closed.
_________________ K. LAKSHMAN, J 12th August, 2024
